behavior.name: github-issues
behavior.summary: Authoritative reference for all GitHub issue operations: reading configuration, querying and creating issues, posting comments via the queue, managing labels, closing issues, and detecting epic parent relationships.
behavior.definition: This behavior consolidates every GitHub issue operation an agent may need to perform. It is the single source of truth for how agents interact with GitHub Issues — from reading and creating issues to posting comments and managing labels. Configuration for GitHub-specific settings is read from .starterpack/config.yaml at runtime.

section.name: configuration
section.rule: Read GitHub settings from .starterpack/config.yaml. This file is project data — read it the same way you would read any project file. If the file does not exist, use the defaults listed below for every key.

The relevant YAML keys and their defaults:
task_source: github: label: "autonomously-nightly" # label used to filter issues for nightly processing
agent_permissions: auto_merge: false # whether to auto-merge PRs after CI passes auto_close: false # whether to close issues directly via gh issue close
Read each key individually. If a key is absent from the file, use the default value shown above. Never fail or abort because a config key is missing.

Wherever this behavior refers to "the nightly label", substitute the value of task_source.github.label from config (default: "autonomously-nightly"). Wherever this behavior refers to "auto_merge" or "auto_close", read those flags from agent_permissions in config (defaults: false for both).

section.name: reading-issues
section.rule:
To read a single issue in full, including its body, labels, state, and comments:
gh issue view {number} --json number,title,body,labels,state,comments
Use this when you have a specific issue number and need complete details.

To list all open issues:
gh issue list --state open --json number,title,body,labels
Use this for a broad scan of open work.

To list open issues filtered by the nightly label (value from config.yaml):
gh issue list --label "{label}" --state open --json number,title,body,labels,createdAt --limit 20
Replace {label} with the value of task_source.github.label from config (default: "autonomously-nightly"). Use this to identify issues queued for automated processing.

To list all open epic issues (for parent detection and dependency checks):
gh issue list --label epic --state open --json number,body
Use this when determining whether a given issue is a child of an open epic.

section.name: creating-issues
section.rule:
To create an epic issue (a parent that groups related child issues):
gh issue create --title "{title}" --body "{body}" --label epic
The body should include a task list of planned child issues. Epic issues use the "epic" label exclusively for type identification — do not add a second type label.

To create a standard (non-epic) issue, use one of the issue type labels:
gh issue create --title "{title}" --body "{body}" --label {type-label}
Valid type labels and their meanings: - enhancement — new feature or improvement to existing functionality - bug — something is broken or behaving incorrectly - task — a defined unit of non-feature work (migration, setup, etc.) - chore — housekeeping, dependency updates, config changes
Choose the label that best describes the nature of the work. The type label also determines the branch name prefix used when work begins on the issue.

section.name: commenting
section.rule: Never use "gh issue comment" directly. All comments must flow through the comment queue so they appear as github-actions[bot] rather than the user's personal account. This is a hard constraint with no exceptions.

The following GitHub issue operations MAY be performed directly (without the comment queue): - Reading issue content: gh issue view {number}, gh issue list - Adding a label: gh issue edit {number} --add-label "{label}" - Removing a label: gh issue edit {number} --remove-label "{label}" - Creating a new issue: gh issue create ...
Everything else — including posting any text that should appear as a comment on an issue — must go through the comment queue.

Append the JSON entry to .github/comment-queue.json. If the file does not exist, create it with an empty array first. The file must remain valid JSON at all times — it is an array of comment objects.
If file does not exist: Write: [] Then append the new entry to the array.
The file after appending must be valid JSON (a proper array).

Commit the updated queue file:
git add .github/comment-queue.json git commit -m "#{number}: queue comment"
Use the issue number of the issue being commented on in the commit message. If queueing comments for multiple issues in one operation, use the most relevant issue number or a comma-separated list.

Push immediately so the comment-sync workflow can pick up the entry and post it to GitHub:
git push
Comments will not appear on GitHub until this push completes and the workflow runs.

section.name: labels
section.rule:
To add a label to an issue:
gh issue edit {number} --add-label "{label}"
This may be done directly — no comment queue needed.

To remove a label from an issue:
gh issue edit {number} --remove-label "{label}"
This may be done directly — no comment queue needed.

Label reference — names, sources, and purposes:
Nightly processing label (name read from config.yaml): Key: task_source.github.label Default: "autonomously-nightly" Purpose: Marks issues to be picked up and executed autonomously. Applied manually by humans or via gh issue edit --add-label.
pending-close: Purpose: Signals that an epic child issue has completed work merged into the epic's feature branch, but cannot close yet. GitHub only auto-closes issues when a PR merges to the default branch (main). Add this label after a child PR merges to a feature branch. The label becomes irrelevant once the epic's final PR merges to main and GitHub auto-closes the issue — no explicit removal needed.
epic: Purpose: Marks an issue as an epic (parent of child issues). Used for filtering and branch-prefix selection. Epic branches use the EPIC/ prefix.
Issue type labels (used for branch naming prefix selection): enhancement → FEAT/ branch prefix bug → BUG/ branch prefix task → TASK/ branch prefix chore → CHORE/ branch prefix

section.name: closing
section.rule:
The standard way to close a GitHub issue is via the PR body, not via a direct close command. Include the appropriate reference keyword in the PR description when creating the pull request:
- PR targeting main: Use "Closes #{number}" in the PR body. GitHub auto-closes the issue when the PR merges to main.
- PR targeting a feature branch (epic child work): Use "Relates to #{number}" in the PR body. Do NOT use "Closes" — that would attempt premature closure before the epic's work is complete. The issue closes when the epic's final PR merges to main.
PR body for work targeting main: ## Summary Adds logout button to the navigation bar.
Closes #42
PR body for work targeting a feature branch: ## Summary Implements session clearing for the auth overhaul.
Relates to #43

section.name: epic-detection
section.rule:
Query all open epics:
gh issue list --label epic --state open --json number,body
Store the result for inspection. If the command returns an empty list, the current issue is standalone — skip to step 4.

For each open epic returned, inspect the epic's body for a reference to the current issue number. A child reference may appear as: - A task list item: "- [ ] #42" or "- [x] #42" - A numbered list: "1. #42" or "1. Fix login crash (#42)" - A prose mention: "child of #15", "part of #15", "see #15" - Any pattern where the issue number appears alongside the epic body text
If the current issue number is found in an epic's body, that epic is the parent. Record the epic's issue number.

If a parent epic is found, determine whether an active feature branch exists for that epic. Look for a branch matching the pattern EPIC/{epic-number}-*:
git branch -r | grep "EPIC/{epic-number}-"
If the feature branch exists: - It becomes the mandatory base branch for the current issue's work. - All branches created for the current issue must be cut from this feature branch, and PRs must target it. - This is not optional — epic children must use their epic's feature branch as the base, not main. - Log: "Issue #{current} is child of epic #{epic}, using base branch EPIC/..."
If no feature branch exists for the epic yet: - The feature branch has not been created. Treat the current issue as if no parent was found and default to main until the feature branch is set up.
If no parent epic is found (or the epic's feature branch does not exist), the issue is standalone. The base branch defaults to main.
